items.title: CC spectral calculus on a Hilbert space with a fixed countable dense sequence

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, spectral representations

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with a specified norm-dense sequence $(d_j)_{j\ge1}$, with
inner product linear in the first argument. Let $A$ be a densely defined
self-adjoint operator on $H$. There is a unique regular projection-valued
Borel measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$ representing $A$, with $E(\mathbb R)=I$,
strong countable additivity, and the exact domain and norm identity

$$D(A)=\{h:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2d\mu_h(\lambda)<\infty\},\qquad \|Ah\|^2=\int\lambda^2d\mu_h,\qquad \mu_h(B)=\langle E(B)h,h\rangle.$$

Here regular means that every finite positive scalar measure $\mu_h$ is
inner regular by compact sets and outer regular by open sets. Every bounded
Borel function $b$ has a uniquely determined bounded operator $b(A)$, with
$\|b(A)\|\le\sup|b|$, $(bc)(A)=b(A)c(A)$ and
$\overline b(A)=b(A)^*$. Every possibly unbounded complex Borel function
$b$ has a closed densely defined multiplication realization with exact domain
$\{h:\int|b|^2d\mu_h<\infty\}$ when $b$ is finite valued; its truncations
converge on that domain. In particular $e^{itA}$ is a strongly continuous
unitary group and

$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac{e^{itA}h-h}{t}=iAh\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h\in D(A).$$

Regular representing PVMs and this calculus transport under unitary
intertwiners. An isometry intertwining the two strongly continuous groups
has a reducing closed range and intertwines their PVMs. These conclusions
use the specified countable dense sequence and CC, with no general
AC spectral theorem, Gelfand representation, Riesz-Markov theorem or Stone
existence theorem as a premise.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary
complex Hilbert space, with inner product linear in the first variable,
and let $A=A^*$ be a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$.
There is no separability or supplied-basis hypothesis on $H$.

There is a unique regular projection-valued Borel measure $E_A$ on
$\mathbb R$ representing $A$, with $E_A(\mathbb R)=I$, strong countable
additivity and

$$D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^2d\mu_x(\lambda)<\infty\},\qquad \|Ax\|^2=\int\lambda^2d\mu_x,\qquad \mu_x(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle.$$

Regularity means compact inner and open outer approximation of each finite
scalar measure $\mu_x$. For bounded Borel $b$, its calculus satisfies
$\|b(A)\|\le\sup|b|$, $(bc)(A)=b(A)c(A)$ and
$\overline b(A)=b(A)^*$. For finite-valued, possibly unbounded complex Borel
$b$, there is a closed densely defined operator $b(A)$ on exactly
$\{x:\int|b|^2d\mu_x<\infty\}$, with norm given by that integral and
convergence of the bounded cutoffs on its domain.

The PVM is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$, and a real $\lambda$ belongs to $\sigma(A)$ exactly when every neighborhood of $\lambda$ has nonzero spectral projection. For $z\notin\sigma(A)$, the bounded resolvent is the multiplier $(\lambda-z)^{-1}$, maps into exactly $D(A)$, and has norm at most $\operatorname{dist}(z,\sigma(A))^{-1}$ (with the zero-space convention $1/\infty=0$).

The operators $U_A(t)=e^{itA}$ form a strongly continuous unitary group on
all of $H$, with the exact derivative criterion

$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac{U_A(t)x-x}{t}\text{ exists in }H\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in D(A),\qquad \left.\frac{d}{dt}U_A(t)x\right|_{t=0}=iAx.$$

They preserve $D(A)$ and its graph norm and commute with $A$ on that domain.
The group with this exact generator is unique. PVMs, Borel calculus and
groups transport under unitary intertwiners, and an isometry intertwining
the groups for all real times has a reducing closed range and intertwines
the PVMs. The construction uses countably generated subspaces attached to
each finite tuple of vectors and their uniquely determined compatible
calculus; it does not choose an arbitrary global cyclic decomposition or
an orthonormal basis of $H$.

items.statement:
Let $a<b$ be real numbers, let $p\in C^2([a,b])$ with $p(x)>0$ for all
$x\in[a,b]$, let $h>0$, put $\theta(x):=\int_a^xp(s)\,ds$ and
$$w_\pm(x):=p(x)^{-1/2}e^{\pm i\theta(x)/h},\qquad q(x):=\frac{3p'(x)^2}{4p(x)^2}-\frac{p''(x)}{2p(x)}.$$
Then:

(a) $w_\pm\in C^2([a,b])$ and $w_\pm''+\dfrac{p^2}{h^2}w_\pm=q\,w_\pm$ pointwise on
$[a,b]$.

(b) The Wronskian $W:=w_+w_-'-w_+'w_-$ equals $-2i/h$ on $[a,b]$.

(c) Let $y\in C^2([a,b])$ solve $y''+\dfrac{p^2}{h^2}y=0$, let
$M(x):=\begin{pmatrix}w_+(x)&w_-(x)\\ w_+'(x)&w_-'(x)\end{pmatrix}$ and
$c(x):=\bigl(c_+(x),c_-(x)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}:=M(x)^{-1}\bigl(y(x),y'(x)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}$
(well defined by (b)). Then $c\in C^1([a,b];\mathbb C^2)$ and $c'=B(x)c$ with
$$B(x)=\frac{q(x)}{W}\begin{pmatrix}w_+(x)w_-(x)&w_-(x)^2\\ -w_+(x)^2&-w_+(x)w_-(x)\end{pmatrix},$$
and with $\|\cdot\|_1$ the $\ell^1$ norm on $\mathbb C^2$ one has
$\|B(x)\|_1=\dfrac{h|q(x)|}{p(x)}$ for every $x\in[a,b]$.

In particular $y=w_+c_++w_-c_-$, and the coefficient system is a nonsingular
linear ODE with explicitly bounded coefficients. No approximation of $y$ and no
physical interpretation is asserted here.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space, let $Y$ be a dense linear subspace of $H$ that is itself
a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $H$ (for instance $Y=D(A_0)$ with the
graph norm of a self-adjoint $A_0$), let $T>0$, and let $A(t)$ for
$t\in[0,T]$ be an operator with $D(A(t))=Y$, self-adjoint as an operator on $H$,
such that $t\mapsto A(t)$ belongs to $C^1([0,T];\mathcal B(Y,H))$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Put $L:=\sup_t\|A'(t)\|_{\mathcal B(Y,H)}$.
Then:

(a) *Existence and uniqueness of a strong propagator.* There is a family
$U(t,s)$, $0\le s\le t\le T$, of unitary operators on $H$ with:
$U(s,s)=I$; $U(t,s)U(s,r)=U(t,r)$; $(t,s)\mapsto U(t,s)\xi$ continuous on
$\{s\le t\}$ for each $\xi\in H$; $U(t,s)Y=Y$ with
$\|U(t,s)y\|_Y\le C_T\|y\|_Y$ for a constant $C_T$ independent of
$(s,t)\in[0,T]^2$; and for every $y\in Y$ the map $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ is $C^1$
in $H$ with
$$i\,\partial_tU(t,s)y=A(t)U(t,s)y,\qquad s\le t\le T.$$

(b) *Uniqueness.* If $V(t,s)$ is another family of bounded linear operators on $H$ with the same strong equation
on $Y$, $V(s,s)=I$ and $\sup_{r}\|V(r,s)y\|_{H}<\infty$, then $V=U$.

(c) *Equations for the reverse and adjoint.* $U(t,s)Y=Y$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$
and $U(s,t):=U(t,s)^{-1}$ satisfies $i\partial_sU(s,t)y=A(s)U(s,t)y$ for
$y\in Y$; $U(t,s)^*=U(s,t)$. Equivalently, differentiating the second
argument of the forward propagator gives $i\partial_sU(t,s)y=-U(t,s)A(s)y$.
The domain maps are jointly strongly continuous in $Y$.

The theorem is stated for the abstract family $A$; a physical generator is
obtained by $A=H_{\mathrm{energy}}/\hbar$ after choosing a time unit.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ a nonempty compact interval, $\hbar>0$, and $\mathcal H:I\to\mathcal B(H)$ a norm-continuous family of bounded self-adjoint operators. Put $A(t)=-i\mathcal H(t)/\hbar$ and $K=\sup_{t\in I}\|A(t)\|<\infty$. For every $s,t\in I$ define $U_0(t,s)=I_H$ and, recursively, the oriented Bochner integrals
$$U_{n+1}(t,s)=\int_s^t A(r)U_n(r,s)\,dr,$$
where $\int_s^t=-\int_t^s$ when $t<s$. Equivalently, for $s\le t$ these are the **latest-time-left** ordered integrals
$$U_n(t,s)=\Bigl(\frac{-i}{\hbar}\Bigr)^n\int_{s<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t}\mathcal H(t_n)\cdots\mathcal H(t_1)\,dt_1\cdots dt_n,$$
with the simplex integral meaning the nested integral with $t_n$ outermost and $t_1$ innermost. For arbitrary $s,t$ its unambiguous nested form is $\int_s^t dr_1\int_s^{r_1}dr_2\cdots\int_s^{r_{n-1}}dr_n\,A(r_1)\cdots A(r_n)$. Then:

(a) $\|U_n(t,s)\|\le(K|t-s|)^n/n!$ for all $n\ge0$ and all $s,t\in I$.

(b) $U(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}U_n(t,s)$ converges in operator norm uniformly on $I\times I$, is jointly norm-continuous, satisfies $U(s,s)=I_H$, and obeys $\|U(t,s)-I_H\|\le e^{K|t-s|}-1$. In particular all original forward-time convergence claims hold.

(c) For every $s,t\in I$,
$$U(t,s)=I_H-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^t\mathcal H(r)U(r,s)\,dr.$$
For fixed $s$ this is the unique continuous $\mathcal B(H)$-valued solution on $I$. More generally, the solution with initial value $C\in\mathcal B(H)$ at $s$ is $U(t,s)C$. For $a<b$, the operator-norm derivatives are
$$\partial_tU(t,s)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\mathcal H(t)U(t,s),\qquad \partial_sU(t,s)=+\frac{i}{\hbar}U(t,s)\mathcal H(s),$$
with the corresponding one-sided derivatives at the endpoints. Therefore, for every $\psi\in H$, $U(t,s)\psi$ is strongly continuously differentiable in either variable and satisfies the same equations applied to $\psi$, with the common bounded-generator domain equal to all of $H$.

(d) Every $U(t,s)$ is unitary, $U(t,s)^*=U(s,t)=U(t,s)^{-1}$, and
$$U(t,s)U(s,r)=U(t,r)\qquad(r,s,t\in I).$$
These conclusions include both orientations of the time interval and intervals containing positive and negative times. If $a=b$, all terms with $n\ge1$ vanish and $U(a,a)=I_H$; the derivative assertions then have no nontrivial interval on which to apply.

No separability hypothesis on $H$, invariant domain for an unbounded operator, differentiability of $\mathcal H$, spectral theorem or physical interpretation is required.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and adopt the hypotheses and corrected latest-time-left notation of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]]: $H$ is an arbitrary complex Hilbert space, $I=[a,b]$ a nonempty compact interval, $\hbar>0$, and $\mathcal H:I\to\mathcal B(H)$ is norm-continuous with bounded self-adjoint values. Write $A(r)=-i\mathcal H(r)/\hbar$, $K=\sup_{r\in I}\|A(r)\|$, $U_0=I_H$, and $U_{n+1}(t,s)=\int_s^tA(r)U_n(r,s)dr$ with oriented integrals. The norm-convergent sum $U=\sum_{n\ge0}U_n$ is the unitary propagator of that supplier. For $N\in\mathbb N_0$, put $R_N(t,s)=U(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^NU_n(t,s)$. Then for all $s,t\in I$:

(a) *Exact oriented remainder.*
$$R_N(t,s)=\int_s^t dr_1\int_s^{r_1}dr_2\cdots\int_s^{r_N}dr_{N+1}\,A(r_1)\cdots A(r_{N+1})U(r_{N+1},s).$$
For $N=0$ this means the single integral $\int_s^tA(r_1)U(r_1,s)dr_1$. For $s\le t$, relabeling $t_j=r_{N+2-j}$ gives the corrected ordered-simplex identity
$$R_N(t,s)=\Bigl(\frac{-i}{\hbar}\Bigr)^{N+1}\int_{s<t_1<\cdots<t_{N+1}<t}\mathcal H(t_{N+1})\cdots\mathcal H(t_1)U(t_1,s)\,dt_1\cdots dt_{N+1},$$
where $t_{N+1}$ is outermost, $t_1$ innermost, and the residual propagator is evaluated at the **earliest** integration time on the right. The universal nested formula specifies signs and operator order for $t<s$ as well.

(b) *Truncation bound.* With $\tau=|t-s|$,
$$\|R_N(t,s)\|\le e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.$$
In fact unitarity under the actual stated self-adjoint hypotheses also gives the stronger bound $\|R_N(t,s)\|\le(K\tau)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$. The original exponential estimate is retained for every $s\le t$.

In particular $\|U(t,s)-I_H-U_1(t,s)\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^2/2$. If the family is scaled to $\lambda\mathcal H(t)$ with a real coupling $\lambda$, the same conclusion holds with $K$ replaced by $|\lambda|K$, so the first-order error is $O(|\lambda|^2\tau^2)$ uniformly when $|\lambda|K\tau$ remains bounded, with explicit multiplier $e^{|\lambda|K\tau}/2$. The stronger bound has multiplier $1/2$. Both time orientations, negative absolute times, $t=s$, $K=0$, the zero Hilbert space and a singleton $I$ are included.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $C$ be the
contour in $\mathbb C$ from $\infty e^{-i\pi/3}$ through $0$ to $\infty e^{i\pi/3}$
and define
$$A(z):=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_Ce^{t^3/3-zt}\,dt .$$
Then:

(a) the integral converges absolutely on compact sets and $A$ is entire with
$A''(z)=zA(z)$;

(b) for real $z$, after deforming each ray to the imaginary axis,
$$A(z)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{i(t^3/3+zt)}\,dt$$
as a convergent oscillatory improper integral. Its first $z$-derivative also
converges uniformly on compact real sets. Higher derivatives are defined by
the absolutely convergent contour representation in (a), or equivalently by
differentiating the oscillatory representation as a distribution; they are
not asserted to be ordinary convergent improper integrals;

(c) as $Z\to+\infty$,
$$A(Z)=\frac1{2\sqrt\pi}Z^{-1/4}e^{-2Z^{3/2}/3}\bigl(1+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),\qquad A'(Z)=-\frac1{2\sqrt\pi}Z^{1/4}e^{-2Z^{3/2}/3}\bigl(1+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr);$$

(d) as $Z\to+\infty$, with $\Theta:=2Z^{3/2}/3+\pi/4$,
$$A(-Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{-1/4}\bigl(\sin\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),\qquad A'(-Z)=-\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{1/4}\bigl(\cos\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr).$$

The error terms are absolute envelope errors and are not relative errors at the
zeros of $A(-Z)$.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary complex Hilbert space, let $H_0$ be self-adjoint on its exact dense domain, and use the resolvent convention $R_0(z)=(z-H_0)^{-1}$. Let $E\in\mathbb R$ be an isolated eigenvalue with $\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_0)\setminus\{E\})\ge g>0$, and suppose its orthogonal spectral projection $P_0=E_{H_0}(\{E\})$ has rank one. Let $V\in\mathcal B(H)$ be self-adjoint with $v=\|V\|>0$, put $H_\lambda=H_0+\lambda V$ on $D(H_0)$, and let $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ satisfy $q=2|\lambda|v/g<1$. Write $\Gamma$ for the counterclockwise circle $|z-E|=g/2$. Then:

(a) $H_\lambda$ is closed and densely defined. For every $z\in\Gamma$, $z-H_\lambda$ is a bijection from $D(H_0)$ onto $H$, with
$$R_\lambda(z)=(z-H_\lambda)^{-1}=R_0(z)\sum_{k\ge0}(\lambda VR_0(z))^k,\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)\|\le\frac{2/g}{1-q},\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)-R_0(z)\|\le\frac{2}{g}\frac{q}{1-q}.$$
The series converges in operator norm uniformly on $\Gamma$ and locally uniformly in the complex disk $|\lambda|<g/(2v)$.

(b) The operator
$$P_\lambda=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma R_\lambda(z)dz$$
is an operator-norm holomorphic, rank-one Riesz projection throughout that disk. Its range lies in $D(H_0)$ and is invariant under $H_\lambda$, and it commutes with $H_\lambda$ on $D(H_0)$. There is exactly one spectral value $E_\lambda$ inside $\Gamma$; it is an eigenvalue of algebraic multiplicity one, with $\operatorname{ran}P_\lambda=\ker(H_\lambda-E_\lambda)$. The function $\lambda\mapsto E_\lambda$ is holomorphic.

(c) $\|P_\lambda-P_0\|\le q/(1-q)$. Rank one holds for every $q<1$, including when this bound is at least one. Whenever two projections $P_\lambda,P_\mu$ have distance less than one, the restrictions $P_\mu|_{\operatorname{ran}P_\lambda}$ and $P_\lambda|_{\operatorname{ran}P_\mu}$ are injective; local comparisons along the path $t\lambda$, $0\le t\le1$, preserve the rank throughout the full disk.

(d) For real $\lambda$, $H_\lambda$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, $E_\lambda$ is real, and $P_\lambda=E_{H_\lambda}(\{E_\lambda\})$ is its orthogonal spectral projection. For complex $\lambda$, $P_\lambda$ is the Riesz projection; self-adjointness or orthogonality is not asserted.

No separability or Axiom of Choice assumption on $H$ is added. Degenerate clusters are outside this rank-one statement.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). To distinguish the Hilbert space from the interacting operator,
write the space as $\mathcal H$, the free operator as $A_0$, and the
interacting operator as $A$. Both are self-adjoint, with
$D(A_0)\subseteq D(A)$. Let $D\subseteq D(A_0)$ be a dense linear
subspace of $\mathcal H$, invariant under $e^{-itA_0}$ for every real $t$.
For every $\psi\in D$, suppose
$b_\psi(t)=(A-A_0)e^{-itA_0}\psi$ is norm-continuous on $\mathbb R$,
and its norm is integrable on both half-lines. Define

$$F(t)=e^{itA}e^{-itA_0}.$$

Then $\Omega_\pm\psi=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}F(t)\psi$ exist on $D$ and,
for every $s\ge0$, satisfy the full original estimates

$$\|\Omega_+\psi-F(s)\psi\|\le\int_s^\infty\|b_\psi(t)\|dt,\qquad \|\Omega_-\psi-F(-s)\psi\|\le\int_{-\infty}^{-s}\|b_\psi(t)\|dt.$$

They extend uniquely to bounded linear isometries on all $\mathcal H$,
with $\Omega_\pm^*\Omega_\pm=I$, injectivity and closed ranges. The
extensions are the full strong limits of $F(t)$ in the two time directions.
No separability, AC, range equality, spectral-type conclusion or asymptotic
completeness is imposed or inferred.

For the consuming intertwining/domain argument, the same construction also
proves the consequence

$$e^{-i\tau A}\Omega_\pm=\Omega_\pm e^{-i\tau A_0},\qquad D(A)\cap\operatorname{ran}\Omega_\pm=\Omega_\pm D(A_0),\qquad A\Omega_\pm\eta=\Omega_\pm A_0\eta\quad(\eta\in D(A_0)).$$

This last displayed domain equality is restricted to the wave range; it
does not assert that $\Omega_\pm$ is onto $\mathcal H$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$H:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Herm}(\mathbb C^d)$ be a map of class $C^2$ into the
Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices, let $P(s)$ be the spectral projection of $H(s)$
for a spectral cluster $\sigma_P(s)$ that is separated from the complementary
spectrum by a uniform gap: $\operatorname{dist}(\sigma_P(s),\sigma(H(s))\setminus\sigma_P(s))\ge g>0$
for all $s\in[0,1]$. Require that the cluster is followed coherently:
$P(s)$ is continuous in operator norm (equivalently, it follows the local
Riesz continuation of its initial cluster). Fix $T>0$. Let $U_T$ solve
$i\,\partial_sU_T(s)=TH(s)U_T(s)$, $U_T(0)=I$
by the finite matrix construction below, and let
$U_A$ solve $i\,\partial_sU_A(s)=\bigl(TH(s)+i[P'(s),P(s)]\bigr)U_A(s)$,
$U_A(0)=I$ (equivalently $U_A'=(-iTH+K)U_A$ with $K=[P',P]$). Then:

(a) $P\in C^2([0,1];\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^d))$ and $K=[P',P]$ is
anti-Hermitian of class $C^1$ with $[K,P]=P'$.

(b) There is a $C^1$ Hermitian $X:[0,1]\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^d)$ with
$[H(s),X(s)]=K(s)$ for all $s$.

(c) *Intertwining.* $P(s)U_A(s)=U_A(s)P(0)$ for all $s$.

(d) *Adiabatic estimate.* With
$C:=2\sup_s\|X(s)\|+\int_0^1\bigl(\|X'(s)\|+\|K(s)\|\|X(s)\|\bigr)ds$ one has
$$\bigl\|(I-P(s))U_T(s)P(0)\bigr\|\le\frac CT\qquad(s\in[0,1]).$$

The estimate is finite-dimensional and conditional on the uniform positive gap;
gap-closing families and unbounded families are not covered.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$H_0=-\Delta$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
([[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]),
let $\mathcal F_2$ be the Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]), so that
$H_0=\mathcal F_2^*M_{4\pi^2|\xi|^2}\mathcal F_2$, and let $t\ne0$. Define, for
$\psi\in L^1\cap L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ and a.e. $x$,
$$(K_t\psi)(x):=(4\pi it)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{i|x-y|^2/(4t)}\psi(y)\,dy,$$
where $(4\pi it)^{-3/2}:=\exp\bigl(-\tfrac32\operatorname{Log}(4\pi it)\bigr)$
is the principal branch ([[def-complex-logarithms-principal-logarithm-and-complex-powers]]).
Then:

(a) $K_t\psi\in L^2$ and $\|K_t\psi\|_2=\|\psi\|_2$; consequently $K_t$ extends
uniquely to a unitary operator $\widehat U_t$ on $L^2$, and
$\widehat U_t=e^{-itH_0}$ in the sense of the functional calculus of the free
operator.

(b) For every $\psi\in L^1\cap L^2$ the representative $K_t\psi$ is
everywhere defined and bounded with
$$\|K_t\psi\|_\infty\le(4\pi|t|)^{-3/2}\|\psi\|_1.$$

(c) For every $\psi\in D(H_0)$ one has $e^{-itH_0}\psi\in D(H_0)$ and
$\|H_0e^{-itH_0}\psi\|_2=\|H_0\psi\|_2$.

No physical interpretation and no point-particle trajectory is asserted.

$V\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ and let $H_0=-\Delta$ with
$D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the free operator
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]), constructed below as the maximal
Fourier multiplier with the $2\pi$ convention. Then:

(a) **Sup-norm interpolation.** There is a constant $C$ such that for every
$u\in H^2(\mathbb R^3)$ and every $R\ge1$,

$$\|u\|_\infty\le C\bigl(R^{3/2}\|u\|_2+R^{-1/2}\|\Delta u\|_2\bigr).$$

(b) **Infinitesimal smallness.** The multiplier $M_V$ with
$D(M_V)=\{u\in L^2:Vu\in L^2\}$ is $H_0$-bounded with relative bound $0$:
for every $\eta>0$ there is $b_\eta<\infty$ such that

$$\|Vu\|_2\le\eta\|H_0u\|_2+b_\eta\|u\|_2\qquad(u\in D(H_0)).$$

(c) **Self-adjointness.** $H=H_0+M_V$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$ and
bounded below.

The potential is real valued but need not be bounded, continuous or compactly
supported; no decay rate is assumed. All original parts (a)-(c) retain this
full potential class and CC alone.

items.statement:
Let $\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z$ be the Pauli matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] (e), acting on
$\mathbb C^2$, and let $\hbar>0$, $\delta,\Omega\in\mathbb R$. Put
$$H:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\delta\sigma_z+\Omega\sigma_x\bigr),\qquad b:=\sqrt{\delta^2+\Omega^2}.$$
Then:

(a) $H^2=\frac{\hbar^2b^2}{4}I$ and the unitary group generated by $-iH/\hbar$ is
$$U(t)=\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{bt}{2}\Bigr)I-\frac{i}{b}\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{bt}{2}\Bigr) \bigl(\delta\sigma_z+\Omega\sigma_x\bigr),$$
which solves $i\hbar U'(t)=HU(t)$, $U(0)=I$; if $b=0$ the formula is read as
$U(t)=I$.

(b) *Squared transition amplitude.* Put $e_{\uparrow}=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}$ and
$e_{\downarrow}=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}$, and use the inner product linear in its
first argument from the Pauli supplier. Define the squared transition amplitude by
$$p_{\downarrow}(t)=\bigl|\langle e_{\downarrow},U(t)e_{\uparrow}\rangle\bigr|^2 =\frac{\Omega^2}{b^2}\sin^2\!\Bigl(\frac{bt}{2}\Bigr)\qquad(b>0).$$
For $b=0$ it is $p_{\downarrow}(t)=0$ for every real $t$.

(c) *Periodicity.* For $b>0$ one has $U(t+2\pi/b)=-U(t)$; the propagator is
$2\pi/b$-periodic up to the central sign $-I$, and every squared transition amplitude
is $2\pi/b$-periodic.

These are the exact mathematical dynamics of the stipulated finite matrix model;
no physical identification of $\delta,\Omega$ with a field or detuning and no
measurement statistics is asserted.

items.statement:
Adopt the hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-allowed-region-wkb-coefficient-equation]]: $p\in
C^2([a,b])$ positive, $h>0$, $\theta(x)=\int_a^xp$, $w_\pm=p^{-1/2}e^{\pm
i\theta/h}$, $q=\frac{3p'^2}{4p^2}-\frac{p''}{2p}$, $M$ the fundamental matrix
of $(w_+,w_-)$ and $c=M^{-1}(y,y')^{\mathsf T}$ the coefficient curve of an exact
solution $y\in C^2([a,b])$ of $y''+\frac{p^2}{h^2}y=0$. Then for every
$x\in[a,b]$:

(a) *Growth bound.* $\|c(x)\|_1\le\|c(a)\|_1\exp\Bigl(h\displaystyle\int_a^x
\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)$.

(b) *Deviation bound.*
$$\|c(x)-c(a)\|_1\le\|c(a)\|_1\Bigl(\exp\Bigl(h\int_a^x\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)-1\Bigr).$$

(c) *Pointwise wavefunction error.* With $\Psi(x):=c_+(a)w_+(x)+c_-(a)w_-(x)$
the leading WKB wave,
$$|y(x)-\Psi(x)|\le p(x)^{-1/2}\|c(a)\|_1\Bigl(\exp\Bigl(h\int_a^x\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)-1\Bigr).$$

The estimate degenerates as $p\to0$ (turning points are excluded by the
hypotheses) and asserts nothing about connecting asymptotics across a turning
point; it is an explicit finite-interval error bound of Gronwall type.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $A$ be the
entire Airy function of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-contour-and-fresnel-normalization]] and
define, for real $z$,
$$B(z):=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\Bigl[\exp\bigl(-t^3/3+zt\bigr)+\sin\bigl(t^3/3+zt\bigr)\Bigr]dt .$$
Then:

(a) $B$ is well defined and smooth on $\mathbb R$, extends to an entire
solution of $B''=zB$, and the Wronskian identity
$$A(z)B'(z)-A'(z)B(z)=\frac1\pi$$
holds for all complex $z$;

(b) as $Z\to+\infty$, with $\Theta=2Z^{3/2}/3+\pi/4$,
$$B(Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{-1/4}e^{2Z^{3/2}/3}\bigl(1+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),\quad B'(Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{1/4}e^{2Z^{3/2}/3}\bigl(1+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),$$
$$B(-Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{-1/4}\bigl(\cos\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),\quad B'(-Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{1/4}\bigl(\sin\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr);$$

(c) *Envelopes.* With $p(z):=1+|z|$ and $S(z):=\frac23(z_+)^{3/2}$ there is a
constant $C<\infty$ with
$$|A(z)|\le Cp(z)^{-1/4}e^{-S(z)},\quad|B(z)|\le Cp(z)^{-1/4}e^{S(z)},\quad |A'(z)|\le Cp(z)^{1/4}e^{-S(z)},\quad|B'(z)|\le Cp(z)^{1/4}e^{S(z)}$$
for all real $z$, and there is $c>0$ with
$A(z)\ge cp(z)^{-1/4}e^{-S(z)}$ for $z\ge0$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be real, let $H_0=-\Delta$ on
$D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, and let $H=H_0+M_V$ be the
self-adjoint operator on $D(H_0)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-l2-potential-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c).
Then:

(a) For every Schwartz function $\psi$
$$\int_0^\infty\bigl\|Ve^{-itH_0}\psi\bigr\|_2\,dt<\infty,\qquad \int_{-\infty}^0\bigl\|Ve^{-itH_0}\psi\bigr\|_2\,dt<\infty.$$

(b) Consequently the wave operators
$\Omega_\pm:=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_0}$ exist as
bounded linear isometries on $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ by
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cook-domain-criterion]], with
$\Omega_\pm e^{-isH_0}=e^{-isH}\Omega_\pm$ and
$H\Omega_\pm\psi=\Omega_\pm H_0\psi$ for $\psi\in D(H_0)$.

(c) *Free absolute continuity.* $H_0$ has purely absolutely continuous
spectrum: for every $\psi\in L^2$ the scalar spectral measure of $H_0$ is
absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, with density
$\frac{\sqrt E}{2(2\pi)^3}\int_{S^2}|\mathcal F_2\psi(\frac{\sqrt E}{2\pi}\Omega)|^2d\sigma(\Omega)$
for almost every $E>0$, using any measurable Fourier representative. This nonnegative density lies in $L^1(0,\infty)$ with integral $\|\psi\|_2^2$, and the measure gives zero mass to $\{0\}$ and to $(-\infty,0)$.
Hence $L^2=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_0)$.

Assertions about the ranges of $\Omega_\pm$, asymptotic completeness or the
S-matrix are not made here; they are separate theorems
([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]]).

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and adopt all
hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cook-domain-criterion]]: $H_0,H$ self-adjoint with
$D(H_0)\subseteq D(H)$, $D\subseteq D(H_0)$ dense and $e^{-itH_0}$-invariant,
$\int_{\text{half-line}}\|(H-H_0)e^{-itH_0}\psi\|dt<\infty$ for $\psi\in D$, and
$\Omega_\pm$ the extensions constructed there. Then:

(a) *Intertwining.* $\Omega_\pm e^{-isH_0}=e^{-isH}\Omega_\pm$ for all
$s\in\mathbb R$, as bounded operators on $H$.

(b) *Domain and commutation.* $\Omega_\pm D(H_0)\subseteq D(H)$ and
$H\Omega_\pm\psi=\Omega_\pm H_0\psi$ for every $\psi\in D(H_0)$.

(c) *Range invariance.* The closed subspace $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_\pm$
is invariant under $e^{-isH}$ for every $s$, and
$e^{-isH}|_{\operatorname{ran}\Omega_\pm}
=\Omega_\pm e^{-isH_0}\Omega_\pm^{-1}$ in the sense of the isometric
identification $\Omega_\pm:H\to\operatorname{ran}\Omega_\pm$.

(d) $\Omega_\pm^*\Omega_\pm=I$, $\|\Omega_\pm\eta\|=\|\eta\|$ for every
$\eta\in H$; no surjectivity onto $H$ and no identification of
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_\pm$ with an absolutely continuous subspace is
asserted.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H_0$ be self-adjoint on its exact dense domain $D(H_0)$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Use $\sigma(H_0)$ for the resolvent spectrum ([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]). Let $E\in\sigma(H_0)$ be isolated, with $\dim\ker(H_0-E)=r\ge1$ and $\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_0)\setminus\{E\})\ge g>0$. Write $P=E_{H_0}(\{E\})$ for its orthogonal spectral projection and $Q=I-P$, using the CC arbitrary-H calculus of [[lem-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cc-arbitrary-hilbert-spectral-calculus]]. Let $V=V^*\in\mathcal B(H)$ with $v=\|V\|>0$, and let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|\lambda|v<g/4$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]). Put $H_\lambda=H_0+\lambda V$ on $D(H_0)$ and assume it is self-adjoint there. Then:

(a) For every real $z$ with $|z-E|+|\lambda|v\le g/2$, the operator $T_\lambda(z)=Q(H_\lambda-z)Q$ **on $QH$**, with domain $QD(H_0)=D(H_0)\cap QH$, has a bounded two-sided inverse $B(z):QH\to QD(H_0)$ with $\|B(z)\|\le4/g$. This includes $z=E$ and the case $QH=\{0\}$, with its unique zero-space inverse.

(b) If such $z$ is an eigenvalue of $H_\lambda$ with eigenvector $\psi\ne0$, then $\varphi=P\psi\ne0$, $\chi=Q\psi=-\lambda B(z)QVP\varphi$, and

$$[EP+\lambda PVP-\lambda^2PVQB(z)QVP]\varphi=z\varphi.$$

(c) Every such eigenvalue satisfies

$$\operatorname{dist}(z,E+\lambda\operatorname{spec}_{PH}(PVP))\le\frac{4\lambda^2v^2}{g},$$

where $\operatorname{spec}_{PH}(PVP)$ is the spectrum of the Hermitian operator $(PVP)|_{PH}$ on the finite-dimensional space $PH$. The statement retains all finite multiplicities $r$ and does not identify any eigenvector of $PVP$ with an exact eigenvector of $V$.

items.statement:
Let $J=[-x_-,x_+]$ with $x_-,x_+>0$, and let $q\in C^5(J;\mathbb R)$ have a single simple zero at $0$:
$q(0)=0$, $q'(0)>0$, $q(x)$ has the sign of $x$, and $q\ne0$ on
[-x_-,0)\cup(0,x_+]$. Let $h>0$ and define
$$\zeta(x):=\operatorname{sign}(x)\Bigl[\frac32\Bigl|\int_0^x\sqrt{|q(s)|}\,ds\Bigr|\Bigr]^{2/3}.$$
Then:

(a) $\zeta\in C^4$, $\zeta(\zeta')^2=q$, $\zeta'>0$ with
$\min\zeta'>0$. Define $a(x):=(\zeta'(x))^{-1/2}$; then $a>0$ is $C^3$;

(b) For each $u\in C^2(J;\mathbb C)$ solving $u''(x)=q(x)u(x)/h^2$ on $J$, define $w:\zeta(J)\to\mathbb C$ by
$$w(y):=\frac{u(\zeta^{-1}(y))}{a(\zeta^{-1}(y))};$$
this is well-defined by (a), and $u(x)=a(x)w(\zeta(x))$. The function $w$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $w''(\zeta)=\bigl[\zeta/h^2+R(\zeta)\bigr]w(\zeta)$ with
$$R(\zeta(x))=-\frac{a''(x)}{a(x)\,(\zeta'(x))^2},$$
where $a''$ denotes the second derivative with respect to $x$; the formula defines a continuous bounded real function on $\zeta([-x_-,x_+])$ through the invertible map $x\mapsto\zeta(x)$;

(c) the constants implicit in (a)–(b) depend only on $q$ and the interval.

$x\in\mathbb R^3$,
$$\psi_t(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{i(k\cdot x-t|k|^2)}a(k)\,dk$$
(the free evolution of the momentum-space amplitude $a$). Let
$K\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be compact with $v/2\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{supp}a$
for every $v\in K$. Then there is a constant $C_K<\infty$ such that
$$\sup_{v\in K}|\psi_t(tv)|\le C_K|t|^{-3/2}\qquad(|t|\ge1).$$
Moreover on every compact set $K'$ with
$K'\cap\{2k:k\in\operatorname{supp}a\}=\varnothing$ and for every integer $N$
there is $C_{K',N}$ with
$\sup_{v\in K'}|\psi_t(tv)|\le C_{K',N}|t|^{-N}$ for $|t|\ge1$.

beams, detectors or measured intensities is made.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space, let $A=A^*\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$\omega\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and put (units $\hbar=1$)
$$H(t):=A+e^{i\omega t}B+e^{-i\omega t}B^*,\qquad H_{\mathrm{avg}}:=A .$$
Let $U(t,s)$ and $U_{\mathrm{avg}}(t,s)$ be the unitary propagators of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]]. Then for all
$s\le t$:
$$\bigl\|U(t,s)-U_{\mathrm{avg}}(t,s)\bigr\|\le\frac{4\|B\|}{|\omega|} \Bigl[1+(t-s)\bigl(\|A\|+2\|B\|\bigr)\Bigr].$$
With $\hbar$ restored, replace $A,B$ by $A/\hbar,B/\hbar$, i.e.
$\|U(t,s)-U_{\mathrm{avg}}(t,s)\|\le\frac{4\|B\|}{\hbar|\omega|}[1+\frac{t-s}{\hbar}(\|A\|+2\|B\|)]$.

The bound is linear in $t-s$; it makes no uniform-in-time claim and no claim
about resonance, decay or an unbounded dipole coupling.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and adopt the
hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]]:
$H_0$ self-adjoint with isolated simple eigenvalue $E$, gap $g>0$, normalized
eigenvector $\psi_0$ with $P_0\psi_0=\psi_0$, $V=V^*\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$v=\|V\|$, and $q=2|\lambda|v/g<1/2$. Write
$Q=I-P_0$, $H_Q=H_0|_{D(H_0)\cap QH}$ on the reducing space $QH$, and define the reduced inverse
$$S=\iota_Q(H_Q-E)^{-1}Q:H\longrightarrow D(H_0)\cap QH,$$
where $\iota_Q:QH\hookrightarrow H$ is the inclusion (and the zero complementary space gives the zero map). Then $S$ is bounded with $\|S\|\le1/g$; no inverse of $H_0-E$ on all of $H$ is asserted. Let $P_\lambda$, $E_\lambda$ be the perturbed projection and
its unique eigenvalue inside the contour, as in
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]]. Define the
gauge-normalized eigenvector
$$\psi(\lambda):=\frac{P_\lambda\psi_0}{\langle P_\lambda\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle}.$$
Then $\psi(\lambda)$ is analytic in $\lambda$ with $\|\psi(\lambda)\|\le3$ for
$q<1/2$, $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle=1$, and $(H_0+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda)=E_\lambda\psi(\lambda)$.
Moreover the first and second coefficients are
$$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_0,\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,$$
where all pairings are finite and the second derivative involves the whole
complementary spectral subspace, not only bound states. Equivalently
$E_\lambda=E+\lambda\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle-\lambda^2\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle+O(\lambda^3)$
for $|\lambda|$ in the disk of the remainder estimate; the $O(\lambda^3)$ is made
explicit in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-analytic-perturbation-remainder]].

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be any complex Hilbert space, let $H_0=H_0^*$ have its
exact dense domain $D(H_0)$, let $\hbar>0$, let $I=[a,b]$, and let
$V:I\to\mathcal B(H)$ be strongly continuous with each $V(t)$ self-adjoint
and $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$. Put $K=v/\hbar$ and

$$E(t)=e^{-itH_0/\hbar},\qquad V_I(t)=E(-t)V(t)E(t),\qquad B(t)=-iV_I(t)/\hbar.$$

The autonomous group is the CC arbitrary-H construction in [F1]. Then
$V_I$ is strongly continuous, self-adjoint, and
$\|V_I(t)\|=\|V(t)\|\le v$.

For $s\le t$, define bounded operators by **vector strong integrals**:

$$D_n(t,s)\psi=(-i/\hbar)^n\int_{s<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t}V_I(t_n)\cdots V_I(t_1)\psi\,dt_1\cdots dt_n,\qquad D_0(t,s)=I.$$

For every fixed vector, these are integrals of continuous $H$-valued
functions on a compact simplex (equivalently iterated integrals). They
define a bounded operator by their action on vectors. This is the meaning
of a strong operator integral; no norm-Bochner integrability into the
Banach space $\mathcal B(H)$ is asserted. The series
$U_I(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}D_n(t,s)$ converges in operator norm uniformly on
the time triangle, with

$$\|D_n(t,s)\|\le\frac{(K(t-s))^n}{n!},\qquad \left\|U_I(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^ND_n(t,s)\right\|\le e^{K(t-s)}\frac{(K(t-s))^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.$$

It extends to all $s,t\in I$ as a strongly continuous unitary evolution,
with genuine inverse $U_I(s,t)=U_I(t,s)^{-1}=U_I(t,s)^*$ and full cocycle.
For every $\psi\in H$ its first-endpoint map is $C^1$ in $H$, with

$$U_I(t,s)\psi=\psi+\int_s^tB(r)U_I(r,s)\psi\,dr,\qquad \partial_tU_I(t,s)\psi=B(t)U_I(t,s)\psi.$$

The second endpoint satisfies
$\partial_sU_I(t,s)\psi=-U_I(t,s)B(s)\psi$. These derivatives are strong
derivatives; operator-norm differentiability is not claimed.

The physical propagator
$U(t,s)=E(t)U_I(t,s)E(-s)$ is unitary, jointly strongly continuous, has
the full cocycle and inverse, and satisfies the vectorwise mild identity

$$U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^tE(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr.$$

For $\psi,\varphi\in D(H_0)$ the scalar curve is continuously
differentiable, with

$$\frac{d}{dt}\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\rangle=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\left[\langle U(t,s)\psi,H_0\varphi\rangle+\langle V(t)U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\rangle\right].$$

The proof actually permits arbitrary initial $\psi\in H$ in this weak
equation. The original statement on $D(H_0)$ is therefore preserved.
No invariance of $D(H_0)$ under the physical $U$, and no strong full
Schrödinger derivative for its domain vectors, is deduced from these
mere strong-continuity hypotheses. In particular, differentiating
$E(t)U_I(t,s)E(-s)\psi$ by an unbounded product rule would require
domain membership which has not been established.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Adopt the
hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]: $H$ is a
complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first variable, $H_0$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(H_0)$, $\hbar>0$,
$V:[a,b]\to\mathcal B(H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and
$v=\sup_t\|V(t)\|<\infty$, $K=v/\hbar$, and $U(t,s)$ is the mild propagator of
that item. Suppose in addition that $(\varphi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete
orthonormal family of $H$ consisting of eigenvectors of $H_0$, with
$H_0\varphi_n=E_n\varphi_n$ and $E_n\in\mathbb R$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]), and
fix indices $a_0,b_0$ and $s\le t$ in $[a,b]$, $\tau:=t-s$. Define the
*transition amplitude*
$$A_{b_0a_0}(t,s):=e^{iE_{b_0}(t-s)/\hbar}\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{a_0},\varphi_{b_0}\bigr\rangle.$$
Then
$$A_{b_0a_0}(t,s)=\delta_{a_0b_0}-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^te^{i(E_{b_0}-E_{a_0})(r-s)/\hbar}\bigl\langle V(r)\varphi_{a_0},\varphi_{b_0}\bigr\rangle\,dr+R_{b_0a_0}(t,s),$$
where the remainder satisfies the explicit bound
$$|R_{b_0a_0}(t,s)|\le e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^2}{2}.$$

Consequently, if $\eta:[a,b]\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ is integrable with
$\|V(t)-V_0(t)\|\le\eta(t)$ for a family $V_0$ of self-adjoint bounded operators,
assume the selected scalar coefficient $c_0(r)=\langle V_0(r)\varphi_{a_0},\varphi_{b_0}\rangle$ is Lebesgue measurable (equivalently here, require it to be integrable). Then the first-order amplitude computed with $V_0$ differs from the exact one by at
most $\frac1\hbar\int_s^t\eta(r)\,dr+e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^2/2$. No physical
transition probability, no measurement postulate and no long-time limit are
asserted.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]] on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space $H$, with inner product linear in the first variable: $H_0$ is self-adjoint on its exact dense domain, $E$ is an isolated simple eigenvalue with gap at least $g>0$, $\psi_0$ is a normalized eigenvector, and $V=V^*$ is bounded with $v=\|V\|$. Let $P_\lambda,E_\lambda$ be the contour projection and eigenvalue, $Q=I-P_0$, $S=\iota_Q(H_0|_{D(H_0)\cap QH}-E)^{-1}Q$ the actual reduced inverse, and $\psi(\lambda)$ the gauge-fixed eigenvector with $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle=1$.

For $v>0$ put $R=g/(8v)$. On the full complex disk $|\lambda|<R$:

(a) $q=2|\lambda|v/g\le1/4$, $\|P_\lambda-P_0\|\le1/3$, $\|\psi(\lambda)\|\le2$, and the holomorphic scalar energy identity is
$$E_\lambda=\langle(H_0+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle=E+\lambda\langle V\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle.$$

(b) The exact coefficients are
$$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_0,\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,$$
with bounds $|E'(0)|\le v$, $\|\psi'(0)\|\le v/g$ and $|E''(0)|\le2v^2/g$. The whole complementary spectral subspace, including its continuum, contributes through $S$. The cubic remainder satisfies
$$\left|E_\lambda-E-\lambda E'(0)-\frac{\lambda^2}{2}E''(0)\right|\le\frac{Rv\,(|\lambda|/R)^3}{1-|\lambda|/R}.$$
At $|\lambda|=R/2$ the displayed bound is $Rv/4=g/32$. For $|\lambda|\le R/2$ it is at most $128v^3|\lambda|^3/g^2$.

(c) If $v=0$, then $V=0$ and $P_\lambda=P_0$, $E_\lambda=E$, $\psi(\lambda)=\psi_0$ for every complex $\lambda$; no radius involving division by $v$ is used in this branch.

These conclusions are conditional on the strict positive gap and bounded perturbation, and do not assert an unbounded or degenerate perturbation theorem.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H_0=-\Delta$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, with domain $H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and let
$$U(s)\psi(x):=e^{-3s/2}\psi(e^{-s}x)\qquad(s\in\mathbb R)$$
be the unitary dilation group. Use the convention $U(s)=e^{-isD}$. Then:

(a) $U$ is strongly continuous and its self-adjoint generator $D$ has $D\psi=-i(x\cdot\nabla+3/2)\psi$ on the core $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$. The unitary position-log map $T_x\psi(\rho,\omega)=e^{3\rho/2}\psi(e^\rho\omega)$ takes $D$ to $-i\partial_\rho$ on $L^2(\mathbb R\times S^2,d\rho\,d\sigma)$, with domain consisting of functions whose weak $\rho$ derivative belongs to $L^2$. The unitary transform $\mathcal G u(\eta,\omega)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-i\eta\rho}u(\rho,\omega)\,d\rho$ takes this operator to multiplication by $\eta$. In momentum-log coordinates the sign reverses: if $\mathcal F_p\psi(p)=(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot x}\psi(x)\,dx$ and $W=\mathcal G T_p\mathcal F_p$, with $T_p$ given by the same polar-log formula, then $WDW^*=M_{-\eta}$, on $\{h:\eta h\in L^2\}$.

(b) With $P_\pm:=\mathbf 1_{(0,\infty)}(\pm D)$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]) one has $P_++P_-=I$. In the $W$ representation these are multiplication by $\mathbf 1_{\eta<0}$ and $\mathbf 1_{\eta>0}$, respectively; the spectral projection of $D$ at $0$ vanishes.

(c) For every $f\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty))$ with $\operatorname{supp}f\subseteq(a^2,b^2)$, $0<a<b$, and every nonnegative integer $N$, there is $C_N$ such that
$$\bigl\|\mathbf 1_{\{|x|<2at\}}e^{-itH_0}f(H_0)P_+\bigr\|\le C_Nt(1+t)^{-N}\qquad(t\ge1),$$
$$\bigl\|\mathbf 1_{\{|x|<2a|t|\}}e^{-itH_0}f(H_0)P_-\bigr\|\le C_N|t|(1+|t|)^{-N}\qquad(t\le-1).$$
Consequently $P_+f(H_0)e^{-itH_0}\to0$ strongly as $t\to-\infty$ and $P_-f(H_0)e^{-itH_0}\to0$ strongly as $t\to+\infty$. The bounds also hold for any integer $N<0$ after enlarging its constant.

references.title: F. W. J. Olver, Asymptotics and Special Functions (1974), Chapter 11 (error bounds for Airy-type Volterra equations near turning points) — classical monograph treatment consulted through the DLMF survey of asymptotics and error bounds

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Adopt the hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-liouville-turning-point-transformation]]: $q\in C^5$
with a single simple zero at $0$, $q'(0)>0$, transformed equation
$w''=[\zeta/h^2+R(\zeta)]w$ on $\zeta([-x_-,x_+])$, $a>0$ the Liouville factor
and $R$ continuous bounded. Put $b:=-\zeta(-x_-)>0$ and $c:=\zeta(x_+)>0$,
so the transformed interval is $[-b,c]$. Let
$A_h(\zeta):=A(\zeta/h^{2/3})$, $B_h(\zeta):=B(\zeta/h^{2/3})$ for the Airy
functions of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-envelopes-and-asymptotic-coefficients]]
(Wronskian $A_hB_h'-A_h'B_h=h^{-2/3}/\pi$), and define the envelopes
$$e_h(\zeta):=\bigl(1+|\zeta|/h^{2/3}\bigr)^{-1/4}\exp\Bigl(-\frac{2(\zeta_+)^{3/2}}{3h}\Bigr),\qquad d_h(\zeta):=h^{-2/3}\bigl(1+|\zeta|/h^{2/3}\bigr)^{1/4}\exp\Bigl(-\frac{2(\zeta_+)^{3/2}}{3h}\Bigr).$$
Then:

(a) *Volterra representation.* For $h$ small the unique solution with Airy terminal data $w(c)=A_h(c)$, $w'(c)=A_h'(c)$ at the right endpoint $\zeta=c$ satisfies
$$w(\zeta)=A_h(\zeta)+\pi h^{2/3}\int_\zeta^c\bigl[A_h(\zeta)B_h(v)-B_h(\zeta)A_h(v)\bigr]R(v)w(v)\,dv .$$

(b) *Stable weighted estimate.* There is a constant $C_A$ with
$|w(\zeta)-A_h(\zeta)|\le C_Ae_h(\zeta)(e^{\varepsilon_h}-1)$ and
$|w'(\zeta)-A_h'(\zeta)|\le C_Ad_h(\zeta)(e^{\varepsilon_h}-1)$, where
$$\varepsilon_h:=Ch\int_{-b}^c\frac{|R(v)|}{\sqrt{|v|+h^{2/3}}}\,dv\le C'h$$
for constants depending only on $q$ and the interval.

(c) *Growing branch and connection.* The solution with terminal data
$(B_h,B_h')$ at $\zeta=0$ obeys the analogous bound with $e_h$ replaced by its
growing analogue on the full interval; consequently, for fixed $\zeta>0$ and
$\zeta<0$ away from zero, the forbidden-side solution
$q^{-1/4}\exp(-\frac1h\int_0^x\sqrt q)$ corresponds to
$2(-q)^{-1/4}\sin(\frac1h\int_x^0\sqrt{-q}+\pi/4)$ on the allowed side, and the
growing forbidden solution to the corresponding cosine, with absolute errors bounded by the envelopes times $C(\varepsilon_h+h/|\zeta|^{3/2})$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\gamma>0$, $H_0=-\Delta$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and
$H_\gamma:=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(H_\gamma)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, the
self-adjoint Coulomb operator established below on this exact domain, with
essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$ as proved by the local compact-resolvent argument. Use the physical-momentum Fourier transform $\mathcal F_pf(p)=(2\pi)^{-3/2}\mathcal F_2f(p/(2\pi))$, unitary by the dilation change of variables, equivalently $(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot x}f(x)dx$ on Schwartz functions. Let $P_j=\mathcal F_p^*M_{p_j}\mathcal F_p=-i\partial_j$ on its maximal weak-derivative domain; thus $H_0=\mathcal F_p^*M_{|p|^2}\mathcal F_p$. Set $a(p)=\gamma/(2|p|)$ for $p\ne0$ and $a(0)=0$, and $a(P)=\mathcal F_p^*M_a\mathcal F_p$ on the maximal multiplier domain. For $|t|\ge1$ define the
Dollard-modified free evolution
$$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}e^{i\,\operatorname{sign}(t)\,a(P)\log|t|}$$
(the two factors commute, being functions of $P$; extend to $|t|\le1$ by
$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}$). Then:

(a) $U_D(t)$ is unitary for every $t$ and strongly continuous in $t$ away from $t=0$; on the dense set of momentum $C_c^\infty$ vectors supported in an annulus $0<a_0\le|p|\le b_0<\infty$ it is differentiable for $|t|>1$, with the exterior one-sided derivatives at $t=\pm1$, and
$$i\,U_D'(t)=\Bigl[H_0-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\qquad(|t|>1).$$

(b) *Integrable remainder.* For every vector $\psi$ in that dense set one has
$$\int_1^\infty\Bigl\|\Bigl[\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\psi\Bigr\|_2dt<\infty,$$
and the same integral with $|t|$ in the comparison denominator over $(-\infty,-1]$ is finite. More precisely, for each such $\psi$ there are $T_\psi\ge1$ and $C_\psi<\infty$ such that for both signs of $t$, $|t|\ge T_\psi$ implies $\|[\gamma/|\cdot|-\gamma/(2|t|\,|P|)]U_D(t)\psi\|_2\le C_\psi(1+\log|t|)/|t|^2$.

No empirical claim, no Rutherford cross-section and no photon interpretation is
asserted; the logarithmic phase is a comparison construction for the
long-range generator.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $m>0$. Let $V\in C_c^5(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$ be fixed and let $E>0$ be such that
$V-E$ has exactly two simple zeros $a<b$, is positive on $(a,b)$ and negative
outside $[a,b]$ with nonvanishing derivative at $a,b$. Set $q(x):=2m(V(x)-E)$
and consider the explicitly parameterized family
$$u_h''(x)=\frac{q(x)}{h^2}u_h(x),\qquad h>0.$$
The quantities and $h$ are nondimensional after fixed scales have been chosen;
the physical reading is the scaled family, with the physical $\hbar$ fixed.
Choose $L>0$ with $\operatorname{supp}V\subset(-L,L)$ and put
$p_0:=\sqrt{2mE}$. Define the scattering amplitudes $r(h),t(h)$ by the exact
solution with one incoming wave from the left and none from the right:
$$u_h(x)=p_0^{-1/2}\bigl(e^{ip_0x/h}+r(h)e^{-ip_0x/h}\bigr)\quad(x\le-L),\qquad u_h(x)=p_0^{-1/2}t(h)e^{ip_0x/h}\quad(x\ge L).$$
Here the conserved dimensionless current is $J_h(u):=h\operatorname{Im}(\overline u\,u')$;
the exterior waves $p_0^{-1/2}e^{\pm ip_0x/h}$ have currents $\pm1$.
The transmission coefficient is the transmitted-to-incoming current ratio
$T(h):=|t(h)|^2$. The proof establishes existence and uniqueness of these
amplitudes. Put $B:=\int_a^b\sqrt{2m(V-E)}\,dx$ and $S:=B/h$. Then there are $h_0>0$, an
$\varepsilon(h)\le Ch$ for $0<h<h_0$, and a constant $C_0$ such that the transmission
coefficient is
$$T(h)=e^{-2S}\bigl[1+O\bigl(\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S}\bigr)\bigr],$$
quantitatively
$$|T(h)e^{2S}-1|\le\frac{C_0[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S}]}{1-C_0[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S}]}$$
whenever the denominator is positive. The bound holds for fixed $V,E$ with the
stated separated simple turning points; rectangular walls, coalescing turning
points, barrier-top uniformity and resonant multiwell interference are excluded.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge1$ be
an integer, $\tau:=s+1$, and let $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$
([[lem-smooth-compactly-supported-functions-are-dense-in-ltwo-of-an-open-set]]).
Write $r=|x|$ and $\Delta$ for the Laplacian. Then
$$\bigl\|r^{-\tau}u\bigr\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}\le\frac2s\bigl\|r^{-\tau+2}\Delta u\bigr\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}.$$
The inequality extends to every compactly supported $H^2$ function that vanishes
in a neighborhood of the origin.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$m,\omega,\hbar>0$, let $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let
$H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}DAD^{-1}$ be the oscillator of
[[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] with
orthonormal eigenbasis $(\psi_n)_{n\ge0}$ and ladder operators
$a_\psi,a_\psi^\dagger,N_\psi$ of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]]
transported to $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$. Work with $\langle u,v\rangle=\int u\overline v$, linear in its first argument, and define $N_\psi^{1/2}$ by the coefficient action $\sqrt n\,c_n$ on $D(N_\psi^{1/2})=\{\psi:\sum_n n|c_n|^2<\infty\}$, where $c_n=\langle\psi,\psi_n\rangle$. Use the negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier convention $\widehat u(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi i x\xi}u(x)\,dx$ on integrable inputs and its Plancherel extension $\mathcal F_2$. Let
$Q=M_x$, $P=\mathcal F_2^*M_{2\pi\hbar\xi}\mathcal F_2$ be the maximal
position and momentum operators (their self-adjointness is proved below), with
$D(Q)=\{\psi:x\psi\in L^2\}$ and
$D(P)=\{\psi:\xi\mathcal F_2\psi\in L^2\}$, with
$H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\frac12I)$ and the couplings
$$Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}(a_\psi+a_\psi^\dagger),\qquad P=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}(a_\psi-a_\psi^\dagger)$$
on the common domain $D(N_\psi^{1/2})$. Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be of class
$C^1$. Put $Y:=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=D(N_\psi)$ with graph norm
$\|\psi\|_Y^2:=\|\psi\|^2+\|H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi\|^2$. Then:

(a) *Ladder bounds.* For every $\psi\in D(N_\psi^{1/2})$,
$$\|Q\psi\|\le\ell\bigl(2\|N_\psi^{1/2}\psi\|^2+\|\psi\|^2\bigr)^{1/2},\qquad \|P\psi\|\le\frac{\hbar}{\ell}\bigl(2\|N_\psi^{1/2}\psi\|^2+\|\psi\|^2\bigr)^{1/2}.$$

(b) *Infinitesimal bound.* For every $\eta>0$ there is $b_\eta<\infty$ with
$\|Q\psi\|\le\eta\|H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi\|+b_\eta\|\psi\|$ for
$\psi\in Y=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$; hence $-f(t)Q$ is
$H_{\mathrm{osc}}$-bounded with relative bound $0$ for every fixed $t$
([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]).

(c) *Common domain.* For every $t\in[a,b]$ the operator
$H(t):=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q$ is self-adjoint on the single domain $Y$
(independent of $t$); moreover $t\mapsto H(t)$ belongs to
$C^1([a,b];\mathcal B(Y,L^2))$ with derivative $-f'(t)Q$, so the family has a
common domain and satisfies the regularity hypothesis of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]].

items.title: Explicit unbounded oscillator propagator

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Chapter 5 pp. 123-131 (unitary dynamics) and Chapter 8 pp. 173-180 (oscillator algebra)

R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Simple Harmonic Oscillator pp. 80-84 (coherent states and the classical solution of the driven oscillator)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Adopt the
notation of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-driven-oscillator-common-domain]]:
$m,\omega,\hbar>0$, $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, $Q,P$ the position and
momentum operators, $H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{P^2}{2m}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}Q^2$ with
domain $Y=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$, $f\in C^1([a,b];\mathbb R)$ and
$H(t)=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q$ self-adjoint on $Y$. For real $q,p$ define the
Weyl operator
$$D(q,p)\psi(x):=e^{ip(x-q/2)/\hbar}\,\psi(x-q).$$
For $s\le t$ in $[a,b]$ let $q(\cdot;s),p(\cdot;s)$ be the unique $C^1$ solution
of $q'=p/m$, $p'=-m\omega^2q+f$, $q(s)=p(s)=0$, and put
$S(t,s):=\int_s^tf(r)q(r)/2\,dr$. Then:

(a) $D(q,p)$ is unitary on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$, preserves $Y$, and on $Y$ the
identities $D(q,p)^*QD(q,p)=Q+qI$, $D(q,p)^*PD(q,p)=P+pI$ hold; along a $C^1$
trajectory $t\mapsto(q(t),p(t))$ one has
$$i\hbar\,\partial_tD(q,p)\psi=\bigl[-p'Q+q'P+\tfrac12(qp'-pq')I\bigr]D(q,p)\psi\quad(\psi\in Y),$$
and the conjugation identity $H_{\mathrm{osc}}D=DH_{\mathrm{osc}}+\bigl[\frac pmP+m\omega^2qQ-\frac{p^2}{2m}-\frac{m\omega^2q^2}{2}\bigr]D$
holds on $Y$.

(b) The family
$$U(t,s):=e^{iS(t,s)/\hbar}D(q(t,s),p(t,s))e^{-i(t-s)H_{\mathrm{osc}}/\hbar}$$
is unitary, $U(s,s)=I$, preserves $Y$, satisfies the strong Schrödinger
equation $i\hbar\,\partial_tU(t,s)\psi=H(t)U(t,s)\psi$ for every $\psi\in Y$,
and provides the unique solution of that equation with $U(s,s)=I$; by density it
gives strongly continuous mild evolution on all of $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$, with
the cocycle property on $[a,b]$.

(c) *Coherent-state check.* Define the coherent vector in the scaled Hermite basis by $\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}z^n\psi_n/\sqrt{n!}$ for $z\in\mathbb C$ (the series converges in $L^2$). If $f\equiv0$, then
$U(t,s)\psi_z=e^{-i\omega(t-s)/2}\psi_{ze^{-i\omega(t-s)}}$, recovering the
undriven dynamics.

No statement about arbitrary unbounded potentials or varying domains is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be real and compactly supported, let
$k>0$, and let $H=-\Delta+M_V$ on $D(H)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$; its self-adjointness
for bounded real $V$ is established below by explicit resolvents. Then $k^2$ is not
an eigenvalue of $H$: if $\psi\in H^2(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies
$-\Delta\psi+V\psi=k^2\psi$, then $\psi=0$.

items.title: Outgoing Fredholm invertibility

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, compact operators and stationary scattering

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $R>0$, let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ with $\operatorname{supp}V\subseteq B_R$,
and put $\mathcal H=L^2(B_R;\mathbb C)$. For $k>0$ define

$$K_kf(x)=\int_{B_R}\frac{e^{ik|x-y|}V(y)f(y)}{4\pi|x-y|}\,dy.$$

Then $K_k$ is compact and $I+K_k$ is boundedly invertible. In particular
$\|(I+K_k)f\|_2\ge\|(I+K_k)^{-1}\|^{-1}\|f\|_2$.
Moreover, on every interval $[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)$ the inverses are
operator-norm continuous and uniformly bounded. Writing $K_\zeta$ for the
same kernel with complex wave number $\zeta$, there is $\delta>0$ such that
$I+K_\zeta$ is invertible whenever $\operatorname{dist}(\zeta,[a,b])<\delta$;
its inverses are uniformly bounded there and converge in operator norm to
the outgoing real-axis inverses as $\zeta\to k\in[a,b]$. For incoming
kernels replace $e^{ik|x-y|}$ by $e^{-ik|x-y|}$; the same conclusions hold.
No zero-energy or high-energy uniform bound is claimed.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ have support in a bounded ball,
$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, $H_0=-\Delta$ and
$H=H_0+M_V$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3)$. Write $R_A(z)=(A-z)^{-1}$.
Use the ordinary wave convention

$$\Omega_\pm=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_0},$$

and the position dilation convention

$$U(s)\psi(x)=e^{-3s/2}\psi(e^{-s}x)=e^{-isD}\psi(x),\qquad P_\pm=\mathbf1_{(0,\infty)}(\pm D).$$

The wave operators exist on all of $\mathcal H$ by the Cook construction;
the dilation operator and projections are those of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-mellin-incoming-and-outgoing-propagation]]. Then:

**(a)** $M_VR_{H_0}(i)$ is compact.

**(b)** For every $f\in C_c(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ with $f(0)=0$, both
$C_\pm=(\Omega_\pm-I)f(H_0)P_\pm$ are compact. This includes the full
continuous cutoff class vanishing at zero, not only smooth positive cutoffs.

**(c)** For every $f\in C_0(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$, $f(H)-f(H_0)$ is compact,
and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(H)=[0,\infty)$. Here essential spectrum means
the real $\lambda$ for which every spectral neighborhood has infinite rank.

**Threshold obstruction.** The hypothesis $f(0)=0$ cannot be omitted in a
uniform theorem over this potential class. For

$$V(x)=-\frac{\pi^2}{4}\mathbf1_{\{|x|<1\}},\qquad f(E)=\max(1-|E|,0),$$

the outgoing defect $C_+$ is not compact. In fact, for this potential it is
not compact for any $f\in C_c(\mathbb R)$ with $f(0)\ne0$.
This obstruction is established by an explicit weakly-null radial dilation
sequence below; no nonresonance or completeness assumption is imposed.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $R>0$, let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ with $\operatorname{supp}V\subseteq B_R$,
let $k>0$ and $d\in S^2$. On $\mathcal H=L^2(B_R;\mathbb C)$ let
$K_kf(x)=\int_{B_R}G_k(x-y)V(y)f(y)dy$, where
$G_k(z)=e^{ik|z|}/(4\pi|z|)$. The supplier
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-outgoing-fredholm-invertibility]] supplies
bounded invertibility of $I+K_k$. Define

$$u=(I+K_k)^{-1}(e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_R}),\qquad \Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}-\int_{B_R}G_k(x-y)V(y)u(y)dy,\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x}.$$

Then:

(a) $\Psi\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$,
$(-\Delta+V-k^2)\Psi=0$ distributionally, and $\Psi|_{B_R}=u$.

(b) With $r=|x|>2R$, $\Omega=x/r$, the smooth amplitude

$$f_k(\Omega)=-\frac1{4\pi}\int_{B_R}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}V(y)u(y)dy$$

satisfies $\Psi=e^{ikd\cdot x}+e^{ikr}f_k(\Omega)/r+\mathcal E(r,\Omega)$.
The error and its first radial derivative are bounded uniformly in $\Omega$
by $C(k,R,\|Vu\|_1)r^{-2}$. For every fixed finite product $D_\Omega$ of
smooth tangential differential operators on $S^2$, also
$|D_\Omega\mathcal E|+|D_\Omega\partial_r\mathcal E|\le C_Dr^{-2}$.

(c) Fix normalization constants $\hbar,m>0$. The scattered radial current is

$$j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)=\frac\hbar m\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}}\,\partial_r\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}})=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f_k(\Omega)|^2}{r^2}+O(r^{-3}),$$

uniformly in $\Omega$. With incident plane-wave flux density
$J_{\mathrm{in}}=\hbar k/m$, the stationary elastic model's differential
cross section is

$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}=\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{r^2j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)}{J_{\mathrm{in}}}=|f_k(\Omega)|^2,\qquad \sigma=\int_{S^2}|f_k|^2d\sigma<\infty.$$

These are conditional model statements. Measured count rates additionally
require incident fluence, target and detector acceptance, efficiency and
background modelling; none is asserted. Part (a) is a local regularity
statement for a stationary scattering wave, with no assertion of membership
in the global $L^2$ operator domain.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be real with $\operatorname{supp}V\subseteq B_R$, let $\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, let $H_0=-\Delta$ and $H=H_0+M_V$ on $D(H)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and define

$$\Omega_\pm=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_0}.$$

These wave operators exist by the concrete Cook construction. Write $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H)$ for the closed span of the eigenspaces, $\mathcal H_{\mathrm c}(H)=\mathcal H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H)^\perp$, and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H),\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)$ for the absolutely continuous and singular continuous spectral subspaces: locally define $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}=\{u:\mu_u\ll dE\}$ and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}=\{u:\mu_u\text{ is atomless and singular to }dE\}$ for the PVM constructed by [[lem-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cc-separable-spectral-calculus]]. Then:

(a) $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_\pm\subseteq\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$;

(b) each wave operator individually is asymptotically complete:

$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_+=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_-=\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=\mathcal H_{\mathrm c}(H);$$

(c) $S=\Omega_+^*\Omega_-$ is unitary on $\mathcal H$ and commutes with $e^{-itH_0}$ for every real $t$.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Born Approximation pp. 211-213 (first Born approximation and its validity condition)
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Chapter 12 pp. 245-256 (Neumann series for the scattering amplitude)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Adopt the
hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-outgoing-integral-and-flux]]: real
$V$ bounded with $\operatorname{supp}V\subseteq B_R$, $k>0$, $d\in S^2$, the
compact operator $K_k$, and write $q:=\|K_k\|$. Then:

(a) *Neumann control.* If $q<1$ then $u=(I+K_k)^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$ satisfies
$$\bigl\|u-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^2(B_R)}\le\frac{q}{1-q}\, \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^2(B_R)}.$$

(b) *First Born amplitude.* Under the same condition $q<1$, with
$f_B(\Omega):=-\frac1{4\pi}\int_{B_R}e^{ik(d-\Omega)\cdot y}V(y)\,dy$ one has,
uniformly in $\Omega\in S^2$,
$$\bigl|f_k(\Omega)-f_B(\Omega)\bigr|\le\frac{\|V\|_\infty|B_R|^{1/2}}{4\pi}\, \frac{q}{1-q}\,\bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^2(B_R)}.$$

(c) *Scaling form.* For $V_\eta=\eta V$ with $|\eta|q<1$, put $K_{k,\eta}=\eta K_k$, $u_\eta=(I+\eta K_k)^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$, and define the corresponding amplitudes by the same integrals. Then
$$\|u_\eta-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_2\le\frac{|\eta|q}{1-|\eta|q}\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_2,$$
$$\sup_{\Omega,d\in S^2}|f_{k,\eta}(\Omega;d)-\eta f_B(\Omega;d)|\le\frac{|\eta|^2\|V\|_\infty|B_R|q}{4\pi(1-|\eta|q)}.$$
This applies to every real $\eta$ in the original real stationary model. For complex $\eta$ the same Neumann construction and amplitude integrals give the same algebraic estimate, without asserting the real-potential flux conclusions. No base condition $q<1$ is needed in (c). These give controlled weak-coupling Born estimates in the actual operator norm, uniformly in both incident and outgoing directions.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$Y:=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with its norm
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]), let
$\gamma\in C^2([0,1];(0,\infty))$ with
$0<\gamma_{\min}\le\gamma(s)\le\gamma_{\max}<\infty$, and put
$$A(s):=-\Delta-\frac{\gamma(s)}{|\cdot|},\qquad D(A(s))=Y .$$
Fix $n\ge1$, let $P_n(s)$ be the spectral projection of $A(s)$ for the
eigenvalue $E_n(s)=-\gamma(s)^2/(4n^2)$ and let $g_n:=\inf_{s\in[0,1]}\operatorname{dist}(E_n(s),\sigma(A(s))\setminus\{E_n(s)\})>0$
be the uniform gap to the rest of the spectrum. Let $U_T$ solve
$i\,\partial_sU_T=T A(s)U_T$, $U_T(0)=I$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]],
with $T$ a slow-time parameter). Then there is a constant $C<\infty$,
depending on $n,\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}$ and the $C^2$ norm of $\gamma$, with
$$\bigl\|(I-P_n(s))U_T(s)P_n(0)\bigr\|\le\frac CT,\qquad s\in[0,1].$$

The theorem is a conditional statement about the external-source Coulomb family
$A(s)$; no laboratory control field, error rate or physical preparation is
asserted, and linear Stark-type couplings are not covered.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$,
$H_0=-\Delta$, $H_\gamma=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and let
$U_D(t)$ be the Dollard-modified evolution of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dollard-integrable-remainder]], with modified wave operators $\Omega_{D\pm}=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_\gamma}U_D(t)$, whose existence on all of $L^2$ is included in the claimed conclusion. Then:

(a) $\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH_0}=e^{-isH_\gamma}\Omega_{D\pm}$ for all $s$;

(b) *Per-channel form.* With the Coulomb angular-radial unitary
$\widehat T_{\gamma,l}$ and its free analogue $\widehat T_{0,l}$ constructed
below with regular coefficient one and density $\sqrt E/(\pi|W_l(\sqrt E)|^2)$, the operator $\Omega_{D\pm}$ acts in
each angular channel as multiplication by a bounded Borel function $b_{l,\pm}(E)$
of the energy;

(c) *Completeness.* $|b_{l,\pm}(E)|=1$ for a.e. $E>0$, hence
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\gamma)=H_{\mathrm{c}}(H_\gamma)$
and the modified scattering operator $S_D=\Omega_{D+}^*\Omega_{D-}$ is unitary
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$.

The statement covers the exactly Coulombic two-body model with $\gamma>0$; it
does not assert explicit scattering amplitudes or measured cross sections.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be real, bounded, central (invariant under
rotations) and supported in $B_R$, let $k>0$, and let $f_k\in C^\infty(S^2)$ be
the scattering amplitude of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-outgoing-integral-and-flux]].
Then:

(a) $f_k$ depends only on $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and its Legendre expansion
$$f_k(\theta)=\frac1{2ik}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\bigl(S_l(k)-1\bigr)P_l(\cos\theta)$$
converges in $L^2(S^2)$ (and absolutely, since $f_k$ is smooth), where
$S_l(k)$ is a unit-modulus number determined by the regular radial solution
$\varphi_l$ normalized by $\varphi_l(r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ and by the outgoing
solution $f_l$ with $f_l(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}(1+O(1/r))$: explicitly
$S_l=\overline{W(\varphi_l,f_l)}/W(\varphi_l,f_l)$ and $S_l=e^{2i\delta_l(k)}$
with the phase shift $\delta_l(k)$ defined modulo $\pi$.

(b) $\bigl|\overline{W(\varphi_l,f_l)}\bigr|=\bigl|W(\varphi_l,f_l)\bigr|$, so
$|S_l|=1$, and the total cross section is
$$\sigma=\frac{\pi}{k^2}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)|S_l-1|^2=\frac{4\pi}{k^2}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\sin^2\delta_l(k),$$
the series converging because $f_k\in L^2(S^2)$ and the expansion in (a) is an
orthogonal expansion.

(c) *Resonance model.* For the single-channel model $S_l(E)=\frac{E-E_r-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_r+i\Gamma/2}$
with $\Gamma>0$ one has $|S_l|=1$ for real $E$ and
$\sin^2\delta_l=\frac{(\Gamma/2)^2}{(E-E_r)^2+(\Gamma/2)^2}$; substituting into
(b) gives the corresponding single-channel cross section. This is a conditional
model calculation, not a theorem that every potential has such a pole.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V=V_2+V_{\mathrm b}$ with real $V_2\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ and real $V_{\mathrm b}\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, and put $H_0=-\Delta$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$. Assume that

$$h(r)=\|M_V(H_0-i)^{-1}\mathbf1_{\{|x|\ge r\}}\|$$

is finite for every $r\ge0$ and belongs to $L^1([0,\infty))$. Then $H=H_0+M_V$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, both ordinary wave operators $\Omega_\pm=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_0}$ exist, $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$, and

$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_+=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_-=\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=\mathcal H_{\mathrm c}(H).$$

Here $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}$ consists of vectors whose scalar PVM measures vanish on every Lebesgue null set; $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}$ consists of vectors with atomless singular scalar measures. The space $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{pp}}$ is the closed span of eigenspaces and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm c}=\mathcal H_{\mathrm{pp}}^\perp$. The scattering operator $S=\Omega_+^*\Omega_-$ is unitary on $L^2$.

In particular, all these conclusions hold for $V=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$, where $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ is compactly supported and $|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ almost everywhere, with $\delta>0$. For this class, for suitable finite constants and all sufficiently large $r$,

$$h(r)\le C_1r^{-1-\delta}+C_2(1+r)^{3/2}e^{-c'r}.$$

Coulomb decay $\delta=0$ does not satisfy this sufficient decay hypothesis; no zero-energy nonresonance or absence-of-zero-eigenvalue hypothesis is imposed.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be real and compactly supported, and set
$H_0=-\Delta$, $H=H_0+M_V$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3)$. Use the independently
constructed complete wave operators

$$\Omega_\pm=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_0},\qquad S=\Omega_+^*\Omega_-,$$

whose individual ranges equal $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=\mathcal H_c(H)$,
as in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]].
The local positive-energy resolvent and outgoing solution are those of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-outgoing-fredholm-invertibility]] and
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-outgoing-integral-and-flux]].
These named supplier inputs must be proved independently; this item does not
establish completeness by assuming its own stationary identification.

Write $\sigma$ for surface measure on $S^2$, normalized by $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$,
$\mathfrak h=L^2(S^2,d\sigma)$, and

$$\widehat g(p)=(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-ip\cdot x}g(x)\,dx,\qquad (F_0g)(E,\omega)=\frac{E^{1/4}}{\sqrt2}\widehat g(\sqrt E\,\omega).$$

For a compactly supported $g\in L^2$ and $E=k^2>0$, let $R_H(E\pm i0)g$
denote the local resolvent limits, and define the free trace on compact sources
and the two stationary transforms by

$$Z_0(E)g=\frac{\sqrt k}{4\pi^{3/2}}\int e^{-ik\omega\cdot x}g(x)\,dx,\qquad Z_\pm(E)g=Z_0(E)\bigl[g-VR_H(E\pm i0)g\bigr].$$

Then:

(a) $F_0$ is a unitary from $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ onto
$\mathcal K=L^2((0,\infty),dE;\mathfrak h)$. The initially defined stationary
transforms extend to $Z_\pm=F_0\Omega_\pm^*$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$; their
restrictions to $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ are unitary onto $\mathcal K$,
they vanish on the pure point subspace, and they diagonalize $H$ as
multiplication by $E$ on its absolutely continuous subspace.

(b) There is a measurable operator-valued unitary $S(E)$ on $\mathfrak h$
such that $F_0SF_0^*=M_{S(E)}$. No generic nonradial potential is assumed to
preserve individual spherical harmonic channels. For $R\in SO(3)$ set
$V_R(x)=V(R^{-1}x)$ and $(U_Ra)(\omega)=a(R^{-1}\omega)$. The covariance is
$S[V_R](E)=U_RS[V](E)U_R^{-1}$, not commutation with $U_R$ for a fixed
nonradial $V$.

(c) Let $u_{k,d}$ be the outgoing stationary solution restricted to a ball
$B$ containing the support of $V$:

$$u_{k,d}=(I+\chi_BR_0(k^2+i0)V)^{-1}\bigl(e^{ikd\cdot x}|_B\bigr),\qquad f_k(\omega,d)=-\frac1{4\pi}\int_Be^{-ik\omega\cdot x}V(x)u_{k,d}(x)\,dx.$$

Here $R_0(z)=(H_0-z)^{-1}$ and $\chi_B$ denotes restriction/localization;
the inverse is the inverse of **$I+K$**, not of $K$. Define
$(\mathcal A_ka)(\omega)=\int_{S^2}f_k(\omega,d)a(d)\,d\sigma(d)$. Then

$$S(E)=I-2\pi i\,Z_0(E)\bigl[V-VR_H(E+i0)V\bigr]Z_0(E)^*=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_k.$$

Adjoints $Z_0(E)^*$ and products in this formula are understood on the
compact interaction region, not as bounded maps into global $L^2$ plane waves.
The right side is norm-continuous on compact positive-energy intervals and
gives a unitary representative for every $E>0$.

(d) If in addition $V$ is radial, the energy-angular fiber decomposes in the
fixed countable spherical harmonic basis as
$S(E)Y_{lm}=S_l(E)Y_{lm}$. For the reduced radial equation

$$-\varphi_l''+\left(\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}+V(r)\right)\varphi_l=k^2\varphi_l,\qquad \varphi_l(r)/r^{l+1}\longrightarrow1,$$

let $f_l$ be the outgoing solution with
$f_l(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}(1+O(r^{-1}))$ outside the interaction region and set
$W_l=W(\varphi_l,f_l)=\varphi_lf_l'-\varphi_l'f_l$. Then

$$S_l(E)=\frac{\overline{W_l(E)}}{W_l(E)},\qquad |S_l(E)|=1.$$

Equivalently, for the real normalized regular solution
$a_l=\sqrt{\rho_l}\,\varphi_l=c_lf_l+d_l\overline f_l$,
$\rho_l=k/(\pi|W_l|^2)$, the multiplier is
$(c_l/d_l)/(c_l^0/d_l^0)$, where the superscript $0$ denotes the corresponding
free normalization. The real regular transforms
$(T_lg)(E)=\int_0^\infty a_l(E,r)g(r)\,dr$ extend to unitaries from the
absolutely continuous reduced radial subspace onto $L^2((0,\infty),dE)$.
They implement the scalar channel statement with the incoming/outgoing phase
factors specified in the proof. No Coulomb continuum transform is used for a
compact potential.

No zero-energy nonresonance, absence of a zero eigenvalue, positivity of the
whole spectrum, finite bound-spectrum assumption, or radiality is imposed on
(a)-(c). The negative and any zero point spectrum are omitted by the
absolutely continuous restriction, rather than falsely declared nonexistent.

items.title: Gap-closing failure

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Two-State System pp. 153-155 (level crossing and breakdown of adiabatic tracking)
T. Kato, Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators, Chapter II.4 (the uniform-gap hypothesis is essential in the adiabatic theorem)

items.statement:
Let $\sigma_z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ on $\mathbb C^2$, with orthonormal basis $e_\uparrow=(1,0)$, $e_\downarrow=(0,1)$. Let $H(s)=s\sigma_z$ for $s\in[-1,1]$, and let $U_T$ solve $iU_T'=TH(s)U_T$, $U_T(-1)=I$, for $T>0$. For $s\ne0$ define $P_+(s)$ to be the spectral projection onto the **ordered upper eigenvalue** $E_+(s)=|s|$.

(a) The eigenvalues are $s$ and $-s$, so their separation $2|s|$ closes at $0$. The uniform positive-gap hypothesis of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-finite-gapped-adiabatic-estimate]] fails.

(b) The ordered upper projection is $P_+(s)=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$ for $s<0$ and $P_+(s)=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ for $s>0$. Its distinct one-sided limits preclude a continuous extension through $0$. At the crossing $H(0)=0$, the spectral projection for its only eigenvalue is $I$, not a distinguished rank-one projection. Assigning any rank-one projection at the crossing does not repair the unequal one-sided limits.

(c) The exact propagator is $U_T(s)=\exp[-iT\sigma_z(s^2-1)/2]$, so $U_T(1)=I$ and

$$\|(I-P_+(1))U_T(1)P_+(-1)\|=1\qquad(T>0).$$

Thus upper-energy tracking fails maximally at the endpoints. This is the ordered branch for which the leakage assertion is made.

(d) There is nevertheless a continuous constant rank-one branch $P_\downarrow=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$ whose vectors obey $H(s)e_\downarrow=-s e_\downarrow$ for every $s$. It starts at energy $+1$ at $s=-1$, ends at energy $-1$ at $s=1$, and satisfies $(I-P_\downarrow)U_T(s)P_\downarrow=0$ for every $s,T$. At $s=0$ this is a subprojection of the degenerate eigenspace; it is not the rank-two full spectral projection $E_{H(0)}(\{0\})$. The original claim that no continuous rank-one eigenbranch can pass through this crossing was false.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the analytic coefficient supplier. Let $H:=\mathbb C\oplus L^2((1,2),dx;\mathbb C)$ with norm $\|c\oplus f\|^2=|c|^2+\int_1^2|f|^2dx$ and inner product linear in the first variable ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). Let $H_0:=0\oplus M_x$ on all of $H$, with $M_xf(x)=xf(x)$. The operator is bounded and self-adjoint, with spectrum $\{0\}\cup[1,2]$; $E=0$ is an isolated simple eigenvalue with gap $g=1$. These assertions and its concrete PVM are verified directly below, without a general AC spectral theorem. Define
$$V(c\oplus f):=\Bigl(\int_1^2f(x)dx\Bigr)\oplus c\mathbf1_{(1,2)}.$$
This example verifies that:

(a) $V$ is bounded and self-adjoint, with $\|V\|=1$. $P_0(c\oplus f)=c\oplus0$ is the projection onto $\mathbb C\oplus\{0\}$, and $\psi_0:=1\oplus0$ is a unit vector with $\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle=0$.

(b) With $Q=I-P_0$, $H_Q=H_0|_{QH}=M_x$ and the actual reduced inverse $S=\iota_Q(H_Q-E)^{-1}Q=0\oplus M_{1/x}$, the second-order coefficient of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]] is exactly
$$\frac{E''(0)}2=-\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle=-\int_1^2\frac{dx}{x}=-\log2<0.$$
The coefficient theorem applies for all complex $|\lambda|<1/4$, where $q=2|\lambda|<1/2$; the first-order coefficient is zero. The contour supplier applies on the larger disk $|\lambda|<1/2$.

(c) The entire second-order coefficient comes from the continuous, indeed absolutely continuous, complementary spectrum of $H_0$ on $[1,2]$. A bound-state-only sum returns $0$, so it misses this nonzero complementary contribution.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Spin Magnetic Resonance pp. 178-180 (rotating-wave approximation and its long-time limitations)

items.statement:
Work on $\mathbb C^2$ with $\hbar=1$. Keep the original commuting example $A=B=\sigma_z$, $\omega=1$, so $H(t)=(1+2\cos t)\sigma_z$ and $H_{\rm avg}=\sigma_z$. The exact and averaged propagators from time $0$ are

$$U(t)=e^{-i(t+2\sin t)\sigma_z},\qquad U_{\rm avg}(t)=e^{-it\sigma_z}.$$

Their norm difference is $2|\sin(\sin t)|$. At $t_n=\pi/2+2\pi n$ it equals $2|\sin1|>0$ for every $n\ge0$. This proves persistent nondecay of the original commuting error. It alone does not disprove uniform-time smallness as the ratio $\|B\|/|\omega|$ becomes small: in the commuting extension $A=\sigma_z$, $B=\beta\sigma_z$, $\beta\in\mathbb R$, $\omega>0$, the exact error satisfies

$$\|U(t)-U_{\rm avg}(t)\|=2\left|\sin\left(\frac\beta\omega\sin\omega t\right)\right|\le\frac{2|\beta|}{\omega}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

To prove the stronger intended general limitation, fix $\omega>0$ and define $\sigma_+=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_-=\sigma_+^*$, $\sigma_x=\sigma_++\sigma_-$. For every integer $n\ge1$, let

$$\varepsilon_n=\omega\sqrt{\frac1{2n}+\frac1{4n^2}},\qquad A_n=0,\qquad B_n=\varepsilon_n\sigma_+,$$

$$H_n(t)=e^{i\omega t}B_n+e^{-i\omega t}B_n^*,\qquad H_{{\rm avg},n}=0.$$

These are smooth bounded self-adjoint Hamiltonians of precisely the form of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-rotating-wave-finite-time-error]]. They are noncommuting in time: for suitable $t,u$, $[H_n(t),H_n(u)]=2i\varepsilon_n^2\sin(\omega(t-u))\sigma_z\ne0$. Their oscillatory coefficient norm satisfies $\|B_n\|/\omega=\varepsilon_n/\omega\to0$. Nevertheless at the growing times $\tau_n=2\pi n/\omega$ their exact propagator obeys $U_n(\tau_n)=-I$, while $U_{{\rm avg},n}(\tau_n)=I$. Thus

$$\|U_n(\tau_n)-U_{{\rm avg},n}(\tau_n)\|=2\qquad(n\ge1).$$

This is the maximum possible norm distance between unitaries. In particular no general bound $\sup_{t\ge0}\|U(t)-U_{\rm avg}(t)\|\le f(\|B\|/\omega)$ with $f(r)\to0$ as $r\to0$ can hold for this whole class, even with $A=0$, fixed positive $\omega$ and dimension two. This does not assert that the finite-time theorem's linear growth rate is sharp; it proves the absence of general uniform-time smallness without additional hypotheses. All assertions concern explicit mathematical models, not a laboratory error or measurement.
